evals.prompt: Create `src/views/support-case.view.ts`: a default grid (subject linking to the record, status, priority, owner, due date), a 'My Open Cases' list, a kanban by status, and a simple edit form. None of the project's files are in this directory: write the file in your answer.
evals.expected_output: One `defineView({ list, form, listViews })` container — never a bare flat view object. `data: { provider: 'object', object: 'support_case' }`, `columns` with `link: true` on `subject`, the owner column is the injected `owner_id` (never an `assigned_to` field), a `listViews.my_open` entry with `filter` triples (`{ field: 'owner_id', operator: 'equals', value: '{current_user_id}' }`), a kanban entry with the required top-level `columns` plus `kanban: { groupByField: 'status' }` (no top-level `groupBy`), and `form` with `type: 'simple'` and `sections` referencing a declared field group.

evals.prompt: Build `src/apps/crm.app.ts`: a Sales group with Leads, Opportunities, the pipeline kanban, a 'My open deals' entry and the sales dashboard; an Approvals group that only shows when approvals are installed; and a second app for the support team, who work the same objects. None of the project's files are in this directory: write the file in your answer.
evals.expected_output: `App.create({...})` with a `navigation` tree of `group` items: `type: 'object'` entries with `objectName`, a `viewName: 'pipeline_kanban'` shortcut, a bare `filters: { owner_id: '{current_user_id}', status: 'open' }` slice for 'My open deals' (no view authored for a one-off), `type: 'dashboard'` with `dashboardName`, and the approvals inbox as `type: 'component', componentRef: 'approvals:inbox'` gated by `requiresService: 'approvals'` (never a `requiresObject` gate on `sys_approval_request`: that object read answers 404 to an approver until a request involves them). At most one app per package, so not a second `App.create` here: the support team shares this product and its objects, so it is a `requiredPermissions`-gated group inside the app. (A support product with objects of its own would carry its app in its own `type: 'module'` package of the suite.) Registered under `defineStack({ apps })`.

evals.prompt: Add a Convert action on `lead` — only for qualified, not-yet-converted leads, from the record header and each list row, launching the `crm_lead_conversion` flow — and a bulk 'Add to campaign' that asks which campaign, for the selected rows.
evals.expected_output: Two `defineAction` items. Convert: `type: 'flow'`, `target: 'crm_lead_conversion'`, `locations: ['record_header', 'list_item']`, `visible: P`record.status == "qualified" && record.is_converted == false`` (bare CEL, never brace-wrapped), `confirmText`, `successMessage`, `refreshAfter: true`. Bulk: `type: 'script'`, `locations: ['list_toolbar']`, a field-backed `params: [{ field: 'campaign_id', objectOverride: 'campaign', required: true }]`, and a `body` that reads `input.selectedIds`.

evals.prompt: Design a custom lead record page: the Convert action inline in the header, a highlights strip, a stage path over `status`, and the related contacts. Also write a user guide for the `crm` package under src/docs and link it from the nav. None of the project's files are in this directory: write the files in your answer.
evals.expected_output: `definePage({ name, label, type: 'record', object: 'lead', template: 'three-column', regions: [...] })` with `page:header` (the declared action's id in `properties.actions`, no sibling action node), `record:highlights`, `record:path` (`statusField`, `stages`), `record:related_list`. The guide is a flat, namespace-prefixed `src/docs/crm_user_guide.md` in pure Markdown (MDX and image references are rejected at build), surfaced by a `type: 'doc'` nav item (`doc: 'crm_user_guide'`).

evals.prompt: Sales reps need a locked-down task workbench: only open tasks, sorted by due date, grid only, no switching to other views; plus a report of opportunity amounts by stage.
evals.expected_output: Capability narrowing is the signal for an interface page: `definePage({ type: 'list', object: 'task', interfaceConfig: { source: 'task', columns: [...], sort: [...], filterBy: [...], userFilters: { element: 'dropdown', ... }, appearance: { allowedVisualizations: ['grid'] }, userActions: {...} } })` — the page IS the view definition (no deprecated source view). The report is `type: 'summary'` selecting `rows` / `values` from a declared `dataset`; there is no `chart` report type.

evals.prompt: Invoice entry as a stepped form — header, then line items, then review — saving the invoice and its lines together.
evals.expected_output: A stepped form over ONE object is `formViews` with `type: 'wizard'` and `sections`, not a screen flow (nothing branches). Line items come from the DATA MODEL: `inlineEdit` on the child's `master_detail` field, which renders the editable grid and saves parent + children in one atomic `/api/v1/batch`; `subforms` only to override derived columns. No custom page, and no 'Add line' button (the ghost row exists).

evals.prompt: Group the opportunity list by stage in pipeline order, and the forecast list by period_label, newest first (period_start is a date).
evals.expected_output: `grouping: { fields: [{ field: 'stage' }] }`: a select keeps its option order, and `orderBy` refuses a select. Forecast: `{ field: 'period_label', orderBy: 'period_start', order: 'desc' }`.

evals.prompt: Make the Reassign Lead toast read 'Lead NAME reassigned'; after Convert's crm_lead_conversion flow completes, open the opportunity it created.
evals.expected_output: `successMessage: 'Lead {{ record.name }} reassigned'` (a `${…}` hole fails `os validate`); Convert gets `onSuccess: { navigate }` ending `${result.output.opportunity_id}`, an `isOutput` flow variable.

evals.prompt: Approve on `contract` should stay visible but greyed until `legal_review_status` is `approved`, and the rep should see why it is greyed.
evals.expected_output: `disabled: P`record.legal_review_status != "approved"`` with `disabledReason: 'An approved legal review is required before approval.'` beside it — an I18nLabel the console shows as the greyed button's hover title; display-only, never a predicate, not a gate. The reason is not written into `description`; omitting the key keeps the default "Not available for this record", and a blank reason or a `*Message` / `*Tooltip` / `*Hint` spelling of the key is refused.

evals.prompt: Give the crm app a Reports entry listing all reports it ships.
evals.expected_output: `{ type: 'report' }` with no `reportName` is the app's report index; the console adds none unless navigation declares it.

evals.prompt: Add a 'Log Call' action on `contact` that asks for the call notes and the outcome in a dialog, and make the dialog's button read Log Call instead of Confirm.
evals.expected_output: One `defineAction` with field-backed `params` (`call_notes`, `call_outcome`) and `submitText: 'Log Call'` beside them — the verb on the param dialog's submit button, an I18nLabel translated at `objects.contact._actions.crm_log_call.submitText`. Not `confirmText` (the message of a param-less action's confirm dialog, refused beside `params`), not `submitLabel` / `confirmLabel` (refused, naming `submitText`), and never blank.

evals.prompt: On `task`, add an 'Attention' list for the signed-in user: their tasks that are open or urgent, in one list.
evals.expected_output: One `listViews.attention` entry, not two views. Its `filter` is a list whose elements all match: one any-of group `{ or: [{ field: 'status', operator: 'equals', value: 'open' }, { field: 'priority', operator: 'equals', value: 'urgent' }] }` beside the rule `{ field: 'owner_id', operator: 'equals', value: '{current_user_id}' }` (the record owner, never an `assigned_to` field). Flat rules only inside the group; no `$or`, `logic` / `conditions` or `anyOf` key.

evals.prompt: `task` already ships `defineView({ list, form })`. Reps want a board: add a `priority` select (A / B / C) to the object and a kanban grouped by it — the list must stay — and tell them what they will see when they first open the board.
evals.expected_output: A new `listViews.priority_kanban` entry (`type: 'kanban'`, the required top-level `columns`, `kanban: { groupByField: 'priority' }`) beside the untouched default `list`, never the list retyped into a board. The hand-over discloses the empty board: every existing task has no `priority` yet, so all of them sit in the trailing `Uncategorized` lane (scroll right on a narrow screen) under one empty lane per option; dragging a card onto a real lane writes the field, or they edit from the list; a runtime-token or CEL `defaultValue` on the new field fills no existing row, and a literal one does only on a SQL datasource, where it becomes the column DEFAULT.

evals.prompt: Add a 'Mark as done' button on `task` records that sets `status` to Done (the option is labelled Done, its value is `done`).
evals.expected_output: A `defineAction`, not a view: `name`, `label: 'Mark as done'`, `objectName: 'task'`, `locations: ['record_header']`, `type: 'script'`, `body: { language: 'js', source: "await ctx.api.object('task').update({ id: ctx.recordId, status: 'done' });", capabilities: ['api.write'] }`, `refreshAfter: true`. The body CALLS the update with the option value: a body that returns `{ status: 'done' }` or assigns to `ctx.record` writes nothing, an `expression` body cannot write, and without `api.write` the sandbox refuses the call.

evals.prompt: Products need a photo wall: every product as a card with its `main_image` as the cover. Write the `listViews` entry.
evals.expected_output: `catalog_gallery: { label: 'Catalogue', type: 'gallery', data, columns: ['name', 'price'], gallery: { coverField: 'main_image' } }` — the kind the request names, added beside the existing views; not a table with an image column, and not the default `list` retyped.

evals.prompt: Add an 'Upgrade' action on `installed_package` that asks for the target version, shows what the upgrade will change before the user confirms (our endpoint `GET /api/v1/packages/{id}/upgrade-plan?version=…` answers `{ success, data: { changes, token } }`), and posts the plan's `token` with the upgrade to `/api/v1/packages/{id}/upgrade`.
evals.expected_output: One `defineAction` (`type: 'api'`, that `target` with `${ctx.recordId}`) whose `params` are `version` and `plan_token` (both `required`; `plan_token` declares no default or carry-over), beside `preflight: { read: { url: '/api/v1/packages/${ctx.recordId}/upgrade-plan?version=${param.version}' }, path: 'data', fields: [{ path: 'changes', label: 'Changes', format: 'json' }], seed: [{ param: 'plan_token', path: 'token' }] }`. The dialog sends that one same-origin GET once `version` has a value, shows `changes` above the params, and fills `plan_token` read-only, so Confirm waits for the answer. Not a script or companion action that fetches the plan by hand, not an absolute URL, credential headers or a non-GET read, and no `result` hole (there is no answer before the read); the endpoint still checks the token.

evals.prompt: Our environment runs our `crm` app and the Service app (`service_desk`, from its own package). Sales reps must not see the Service app; service agents use it daily. The customer also asks that each position lands on its own app by default. What do we author?
evals.expected_output: `tabPermissions: { service_desk: 'hidden' }` (keyed by the app's `name`) on a permission set the sales position distributes. The app leaves the reps' Home tiles, App Switcher and `GET /api/v1/me/apps`. That is visibility, not access: the app's URL still opens, and any other value for it on another set a rep holds (`visible`, `default_on`, `default_off`) outranks `hidden`, so the set everyone holds must carry no `tabPermissions` entry for it. If reps must not open it at all, the Service app declares `requiredPermissions: ['service.access']` and the agents' permission set grants `systemPermissions: ['service.access']`; admins need that grant too. Not the app's own `hidden` flag, which takes it off the switcher for everyone. A per-position default app does not exist (an app's `isDefault` is global): say so, promise none.

evals.prompt: Sales reps add lines to an invoice from a header button: they pick a `product` and a `quantity`. Reps can neither read nor edit a price. `invoice_line.amount` is a stored `expression` (`record.quantity * record.unit_price`), and the line's `product` lookup declares `lookupAutofill` from the product's `list_price`. Author the action.
evals.expected_output: One `defineAction` (`type: 'script'`, `objectName: 'invoice'`) whose `params` are `product` and `quantity`, each borrowed with `objectOverride: 'invoice_line'`, and whose `body` (`capabilities: ['api.read', 'api.write']`) reads `ctx.api.object('product').findOne({ where: { id: input.product } })` and inserts the line with `invoice: ctx.recordId` and `unit_price: product.list_price`. `lookupAutofill` fills only the form and the grid, and the stored expression reads only its own row, so an insert that sends no `unit_price` stores no `amount`. The body runs trusted, so it reads the price the rep cannot. If lines are also written by the API, an import or an agent, a `beforeInsert` hook on `invoice_line` copies the price instead.

evals.prompt: Author the default form view for `opportunity`: 42 fields in six sections (Basics, Amounts, Dates, Partner, Shipping, Internal Notes). Reps fill Basics and Amounts on every create and the other four rarely. The form opens in the New dialog, mostly on wide screens.
evals.expected_output: One form view with `type: 'simple'`: the six sections stacked on one scrolling page, each listing its own `fields`, with `collapsed: true` on the four rarely filled ones (or `collapse: 'collapsed'` on those `fieldGroups` entries of the object). `columns: 3` uses the wide dialog and `modalSize: 'xl'` sizes it. Not tabs: a required field on another tab is flagged only on its tab, and the tab strip overflows on a phone.

evals.prompt: The `submit_signoff` script action on `crm_invoice` refuses a non-draft invoice with `throw new Error('Only a draft invoice can be signed off.')` in its `js` body, so zh-CN users read that English sentence in the failure toast. Make it refuse in the caller's language, with the code `NOT_DRAFT` and a 409.
evals.expected_output: The action declares `refusals: { NOT_DRAFT: { message: 'Only a draft invoice can be signed off.', status: 409 } }` and the body throws the code instead of the sentence: `throw { code: 'NOT_DRAFT' }`. The server answers the declared sentence on the refusal's `userMessage` with status 409, in the caller's locale once the zh-CN bundle carries `objects.crm_invoice._actions.submit_signoff.refusals.NOT_DRAFT.message`, else as declared, and the console's failure toast shows it. The action authors no failure copy of its own, which would replace that sentence in the toast. A code the body throws literally and `refusals` does not declare is refused at save. Not a locale branch in the body, and not a second sentence per language in the throw.

evals.prompt: The `send_email` script action on `crm_contact` logs a `crm_activity` whose subject its `js` body builds as `'Email: ' + input.subject`. Our organization works in zh-CN, but every logged subject reads English. Make the subject follow the organization's language.
evals.expected_output: The action declares `texts: { email_subject: { message: 'Email: {{ subject }}', params: ['subject'] } }` and the body writes `const subject = await ctx.text('email_subject', { subject: input.subject });` instead of concatenating. The sentence is answered in the organization's language (the Localization setting if somebody set it, else `i18n.defaultLocale`), never the language of the person who pressed the button, and translated at `objects.crm_contact._actions.send_email.texts.email_subject.message`, the translation keeping its `{{ subject }}` hole. With no translation the declared sentence is written. A key `texts` does not declare is refused. Not a locale branch in the body, and not a `messages` lookup.

evals.prompt: The `import_contacts` api action on `crm_contact` returns `{ imported: 12, rejected: [{ email, reason }, ...] }` as its `result.data`. When it finishes, show the user how many contacts were imported and every rejected row with its email and reason. Write the part of the action that does this.
evals.expected_output: The action declares `resultDialog: { fields: [{ path: 'imported', label: 'Imported', format: 'text' }, { path: 'rejected', label: 'Rejected', format: 'table', columns: [{ path: 'email', label: 'Email' }, { path: 'reason', label: 'Reason' }] }] }`. `table` is a field format: one row per element of the array at `path`, one cell per `columns` entry in order, each column an object whose `path` is read inside one element. `columns` is required with `table` and never guessed from the element's keys. Not a dialog-level `format: 'table'`, not a list of column names, not a `successMessage` that spells the rows out (the dialog replaces the toast), and no promise of a copy button on a text cell.
